stories.caption:
MISSION BRIEF // F10 LIGHTRUNNER / SKYDIO

//Skydio

Tech: Autonomy

Platform: Fixed-wing aircraft

Goal: Give emergency response, search and rescue, and asset inspection teams fast aerial coverage over long distances.

Why: Skydio says a single MegaDock with the F10's 30-mile flight radius covers nearly 3,000 square miles from one launch location.

Traction: Scheduled to deploy to customers in 2027, per Skydio.

Skydio's F10 Lightrunner is the company's first fixed-wing aircraft. It uses a Robotic Takeoff and Landing system that launches and catches the aircraft, and a MegaDock can house up to five F10s so a team can run concurrent missions. The aircraft is designed to fly at speeds up to 100 mph, includes an integrated parachute, and is built to launch and land in significant wind and at night.

Source: Skydio, Inc., 24SEP26

Image: skydio.com (courtesy)

fields.benefit_headline:
IT FINDS DRONES
AND STRIKES THEM

frames.mediaQuery: VAMPIRE counter-drone kit L3Harris U.S. Navy

stories.caption:
MISSION BRIEF // VAMPIRE

//L3Harris

📍Melbourne, FL

Tech: Precision strike

Platform: Portable counter-drone kit

Goal: Defeat drones and remotely piloted platforms in littoral waters for the U.S. Navy.

Why: The kit is self-contained and can be installed on most vehicles with a cargo bed.

Ticker: NYSE: LHX

Traction: Selected by the U.S. Navy to deliver VAMPIRE systems, and delivering to the U.S. Army, per L3Harris.

L3Harris Technologies said on Sept. 8, 2026 that the U.S. Navy picked it to deliver VAMPIRE counter-unmanned systems as part of the service's integrated counter-UxS defense architecture. The company says it is building new capabilities into VAMPIRE to fit different customer missions and hardening the system against the stresses of maritime environments, in the words of company president Tony Calderon, "VAMPIRE is a flexible and effective system that meets the unique requirements of the U.S. Navy for littoral C-UxS defense."

VAMPIRE pairs reconnaissance with precision strike against drones and remotely piloted platforms across domains. L3Harris describes the launch kit as portable and fitted to most vehicles with a cargo bed, where it can fire APKWS or other laser-guided munitions.

Separately, L3Harris unveiled its Wraith Shield software earlier in 2026. It turns a radio into a sensor that can detect small drones, and it can be paired with VAMPIRE and Drone Guardian systems for layered defense.

Source: L3Harris Technologies, 08SEP26

Image: L3Harris (courtesy)

stories.caption:
MISSION BRIEF // LIGHTFISH / SEASATS

//Seasats

📍San Diego, CA

Tech: Autonomous surveillance

Platform: Unmanned surface vessel

Goal: Detect illegal maritime activity, including drug trafficking and unauthorized vessel ingress, in U.S. waters.

Why: The vessels operate without a crew aboard and can be launched by two people from a boat ramp or a pickup truck.

Backers: Shield Capital, L3Harris Technologies, Konvoy Ventures

Traction: Lightfish vessels have operated on the Rio Grande since January 2026, per Seasats. Seasats announced a fleet deployed from the Texas coast into the Gulf of America.

Each Lightfish is about 11 feet long and weighs 340 pounds. The vessels run on solar power and can stay on station for multiple months. Sensor payloads in a modular bay have included electro-optical and infrared cameras, signals payloads and sonar, letting one hull be set up for different sensing jobs.

Seasats CEO Mike Flanigan described the Gulf fleet as an expansion of an existing autonomous surveillance effort tied to the Homeland Defense and Americas Security Affairs office, saying the vessels act as a continuous watch on the water. "Operating autonomously and without a crew aboard" is how the company describes the fleet's design.

Source: Seasats via PR Newswire, 2 Oct 2026

Image: U.S. Army photo by Spc. Jacob D. Harrell

The appearance of U.S. Department of War (DoW) visual information does not imply or constitute DoW endorsement.

stories.caption:
MISSION BRIEF // EAGLEEYE / ANDURIL

//Anduril Industries

Tech: AI-enhanced vision

Platform: Helmet-mounted system

Goal: Give warfighters digital vision, threat detection and connectivity in combat.

Why: Operators can hand off control of unmanned vehicles, request artillery support and command robotic teammates without lowering their gaze from the environment around them.

Traction: Described on the company's EagleEye product page, which lists a family of warfighter augments powered by Lattice.

EagleEye is a family of warfighter augments powered by Lattice, Anduril's software platform. The system combines AI-enhanced digital vision, Blue Force tracking and 6DOF spatial awareness overlaid on the real world. Its sensing suite adds RF detection, rearview cameras, non-emissive lasers, biometric and environmental sensors, and alerts that reach operators as the battlefield changes.

Listed hardware includes 1 km threat detection with optical zoom EO and LWIR cameras, four 4K uOLED displays, and an 8-microphone array for gunshot and drone detection and localization. A collaborative 3D sand table supports mission command, remote planning and mission rehearsal.

Anduril Industries describes itself as a defense technology company focused on autonomous systems, and calls Lattice the software layer behind its software-defined weapons, one that plugs into third-party and government-owned capabilities.

Source: Anduril Industries, undated product page (anduril.com/eagleeye)

Image: Anduril (courtesy)

stories.caption:
MISSION BRIEF // COYOTE BLOCK 2C+RM / RAYTHEON

//Raytheon

📍Arlington, VA

Tech: Counter-drone interceptor

Platform: Interceptor upgrade

Goal: Counter current and emerging drone threats with a new seeker, warhead and rocket motor for faster launch and flight.

Why: Faster successive shots are meant to shorten threat engagement times.

Ticker: NYSE: RTX

Traction: Three Raytheon-funded developmental tests completed, with first launches of a Coyote effector equipped with a tactical rocket motor, per RTX. The upgrade builds on current Coyote variants, which have intercepted hundreds of drones in combat.

Raytheon, an RTX business, says the Coyote Block 2C+RM program advanced from concept to testing in 15 months. The company said the tests also confirmed initial integration with the current counter-drone architecture. The effort is intended to support an urgent joint U.S. military mission against evolving drone threats.

Source: RTX, October 12, 2026

Image: RTX (courtesy)
